Comments: On 6/7/22 at 1305 hrs., I conducted a follow up inspection of Stonehaven Energy Mgt. Co., LLC's Lott 2 well (API 065-26057) in Henderson Twp., Jefferson Co. A Notice of Violation was issued after an inspection conducted by WQSS Shank on 5/19/22 in which a production fluid release was documented (inspection ID 3365343, enforcement 403932). The area around the production fluid tank appears to have fresh pea gravel and spent absorbent pads are still present at the base of the poly tank. The area of the well pad around the well head still remains stained, with signs of stressed and potentially dead vegetation. This area was previously shown to have soil conductivity greater than 20 mS/cm. Additional excavation should be conducted to properly remediate the site. No written response to the NOV issued on 5/24/22 has been received by the Department. No disposal receipts for impacted material has been received by the Department. Violations from inspection ID 3365343 remain outstanding and are being cited again for this inspection. An additional violation of 91.33(b) is being cited for failure to remove residual substances from the ground within 15 days of a pollution incident.

Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an incident response inspection that was conducted on-site.Kris Bowser with AMS Energy contacted me on Thursday, July 14, 2022, to report a brine spill that had occurred on AMS's Barrett Pattison 5 Well Site. The spill had been discovered earlier the same day. A valve had been broken off of a fiberglass brine tank that was used on-site. Kris believed that the valve had likely been damaged by an ATV that had gotten too close to the tank. Fluid from the tank had recently been hauled out. Kris estimated that less than a barrel of brine had been spilled onto the ground near the tank.Kris met me on-site to view the spill. The damaged valve had been repaired. Most of the spilled brine appeared to have settled in a swale that ran next to the tank. The impacted area was clearly marked with dead vegetation. My soil conductivity probe was used to verify the extent of the impacted area. Elevated readings were not observed beyond the area marked by the dead vegetation. A plan for addressing the impacted soil was discussed with Kris. The soil should be excavated and hauled to a landfill. Kris indicated the AMS would provide the Department with a receipt of disposal from the landfill once the soil has been disposed of.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/14/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 913920
Permit API: 085-23966
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: Hempfield Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/14/2021
Comments: Stopped to investigate this complaint of oil overflowing a tank. Alan Wolf (DEP) was present. It was evident that the plastic brine tank had overflowed (no top lid and oil residue on top of tank and on the sides). There was oil saturated hay inside the diking. There was about 3 to 20 gallons of oil still in the diking. There was oil staining on the high ends of the inside of the diking indicating a significant fluid level that was once present and had dropped. The metal stock tank #64411, was about 1/4 full. The poly (brine) tank was also 1/4 full. There was stressed vegetation on the outside of the diking in roughly a 12' x 3' area. The conductivity was high in this area (20,000 micro siemens/cm with soil conductivity probe). The soil conductivity probe showed areas on average of 5,000 micro siemens/cm inside the diking about one foot deep. The gas well was producing with the annulus buried. The well was tagged. It had house gas plumbed off the 4" casing at the well with two regulators and a meter.

Comments: Routine inspection to conduct sampling at the established routine monitoring points. DEP Compliance Specialist Chris Southard accompanied me on this inspection. The wells are now in production. The Modular Aboveground Storage Structure (MASS) was being emptied at the time of this inspection in preparation for its disassembly. A battery of frac tanks remains within secondary containment on the pad. Seven samples were collected at seven of the monitoring points. The location of the SW-2 monitoring point did not have enough water to collect so no water was collected here. A hose was connected to the PVC pipe and was spraying water inside and outside of the secondary containment under the PVC pipe outlet. This containment was also overflowing at the time of this inspection. After we sampled from the pipe, we reattached the hose and it did not leak after that. Outstanding violations.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 11/30/2023
Comments: On 11/30/2023, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Stech F69 well. The following was observed:The well and operator's information were posted onsite (Photos 1, 2).The wellhead, production equipment, and production tank were in generally good condition. Some corrosion noted, loose wires/equipment near wellhead (Photos 3-6). Tank fluids high - I recommend pumping fluid out and placing lid on tank (Photo 7).Silt fence in the woods below production tank. I recommend ensuring that no sediment from the site washes downslope towards the tributary below (Photo 8).The access road was in poor condition leading the whole way to the site from the main road (Photos 9-25 with specific locations). Several areas displayed lack of maintenence and drainage concerns seen by pooling, potholes, channelization, and accelerated erosion. Culverts that run under the road leading to tributary to Pigeon Creek appeared to require clean out and outlet protection - erosion at outlets. There was a section of the access road closer to the entrance gate that displayed undercutting and failure along the guardrail. The integrity of the access road appeared jeopardized and may progress with repeated rain events and heavy truck traffic. The road does not display a safe way for emergency vehicles to navigate in case of emergency at the wellsite.Observations communicated to operator via phone on 11/30/23.Due to the poor condition of the access road and lack of maintenance, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), 78.53, and 102.22(a)2ii are being issued.

Comments: On September 18, 2024 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well Site located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3774486 where violations were issued for an 18-20 barrel release of production fluid from a production tank on June 4, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the production tank that was leaking during IR 3774486 has since been removed from the well site. A well tag was fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it, and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges was observed coming from or near the wellhead. The area where the production tank once (where the spill originated), the slope that the spill traveled down, and the area downstream where the spill pooled up at now appears to be backfilled, seeded and mulched pending vegetative growth. In addition, at the edge of the downslope area right before a forested area began, some black fencing was observed.Several soil conductivity readings were taken in the spill areas (0.0418 mS, 0.0362 mS, 0.0054 mS, 0.0137 mS, and 0.0602 mS) and are significantly lower than the soil conductivity readings taken in the same areas at the time of the spill (Soil conductivity readings taken on 6/4/24 documented in IR 3774486: 1.35 mS, 1.454 mS, Over Range, 7.63 mS, 5.51 mS, and 4.90 mS). Upon inspection of the fence, two areas appeared to be compromised. A stake appeared to be snapped and the fence appeared to be pushed down by sediment, at this time, there did not appear to be any evidence of the sediment overtopping the fence and no erosion or sedimentation was observed behind this section of fence. Another section of the fence right behind a small tree appeared to not be trenched and a gap was observed between the bottom of the fence and the ground. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed behind this section of the fence a this time either.The Department is recommending the Operator promptly properly implement and maintain the temporary erosion and sedimentation (E and S) best management practices (BMPs) to prevent any pollution from occurring.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly implement and maintain E and S BMPs. In addition, violations issued during IR 3774486 shall remain outstanding until the Act 2 Report is submitted, received, reviewed and approved by the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARG RESOURCES INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/07/2021
Violation Code: 78.64(a) - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For a tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator failed to construct and maintain a dike or other method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112.
Violation ID: 920345
Permit API: 047-23879
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Highland Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/07/2021
Comments: This inspection focuses on multiple discharges from various tanks that are located in the proximity of this well. An approximate 210 bbl portable steel stock tank is actively discharging crude oil from a corroded part of the tank. The fluid is currently discharging at a minimal rate and likely only occurs during hot, sunny conditions which liquifies the residual paraffin at the bottom of the tank. At this time, there is approximately 10 gallons of free crude near the tank and a 5' x 10' area of oil soaked ground downslope of the discharge point. A second tank with the same issues is located to the south of this well. The nipple located on the bottom of a steel stock tank located west of this well has failed and resulted in an approximate 1/2 barrel of crude oil to discharge onto the ground, within an earthen containment. GPS coordinates of these incident sites are provided in the photographs included in this report. The well itself is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the location.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/03/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 105.11(a) - PERMIT REQUIREMENTS – Person failed to obtain a permit from the Department prior to construction, operation, maintenance, modification, enlargement or abandonment of a water obstruction or encroachment.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/03/2026
Violation Code: 105.11(a) - PERMIT REQUIREMENTS – Person failed to obtain a permit from the Department prior to construction, operation, maintenance, modification, enlargement or abandonment of a water obstruction or encroachment.
Violation ID: 8284095
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Cogan House Twp, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/15/2023 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Cogan House Twp, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/15/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 988203
Permit API: 081-21298
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/15/2023
Comments: On March 15, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection (CTS No. 370596) at the Range Resources Laurel Hill Well Pad G. Kirby Steck with Range Resources reported a spill of about 15-20 gallons of produced fluid from a rolloff dumpster located on the pad from a recent clean out service of the 9H Well on March 14, 2023. There was some residual produced fluid remaining in the containment from the clean out equipment that was placed in the dumpster and overwhelmed the secondary containment the dumpster was located in. The produced fluid was spilled on the well pad surface. Range Resources began removing the impacted soil on the evening of March 14, 2023. Range Resources excavated the top surface of the well pad of an area of about 40 ft. x 30 ft. The DEP attempted to screen the area of excavation with a soil conductivity meter but the ground was too frozen to acquire a reading. Mr. Steck said that Range Resources needs to remove a small amount of impacted soil next to the roll off dumpster but the equipment onsite was not able to complete the excavation. Equipment small enough to finish the excavation is planned to arrive on March 15, 2023.DEP spoke with Mr. Steck around 1300 on March 15, 2023 and he said the additional rolloff dumpster arrived. Range Resources was able to finish the excavation and add the impacted soil into the dumpster. Containment for this rolloff dumpster was in route to the site.The spill of produced fluid outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Stream Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. The violations noted have been immediately corrected.

Permit API: 117-21998
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-06-18
Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to assess overall site conditions on and off the pad. I was accompanied by Sasha Minium, DEP WQS Supervisor for this inspection. Heavy rain within the hours preceding this inspection caused there to be a large amount of water sitting on the pad surface, flowing from the PVC pipe to the west of the pad, and in the wetland and Salt Spring Run to the west of the pad. The 2H and 4H wells are still in flowback. Conductivity readings near the MASS were below 0.8 mS/cm. Taylor Parsons of Falcon accompanied us while we screened the pad surface for conductivity. Conductivities on the pad surface were less than 500 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was on location during the inspection removing water from the pad surface. A work crew was in the process of attaching plumbing from the well heads to the production equipment. A water sample and a conductivity reading was taken from each monitoring point with the exception of SW-6, the wetland near Salt Spring Run, and SW-7, the confluence of the wetland and Salt Spring Run, due to the high volume of water in Salt Spring Run and the wetland and due to the swift current in Salt Spring Run. Outstanding violations.

Violation ID: 8243837
Permit API: 015-23892
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/07/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Columbia, Springfield and Troy Townships, Bradford County on 8/7/2025 at 0900 hours. The weather was 68 degrees F with mostly clear skies. The inspection was conducted to assess ongoing remedial activities after a well control incident on 7/13/2025 resulted in a produced fluids release.Repsol continues to conduct remedial activities. Some scraping and removal of pad material around the western corner of the pad surface has been conducted. Materials removed from the pad and soils removed from impacted areas downslope are being stored within a secondary containment structure on the pad (photo #1). Repsol has obtained approval to dispose of impacted materials at a landfill. A rain event occurred on Thursday, 7/31/2025. Stormwater and fluids are being diverted into the lined detention basin located downslope of the pad (photo #12). Less than 6 inches of fluids were observed in the basin today. Drain tile piping has been installed downslope of the majority of the pad's fill slopes (photos #2, 3, 7 and 9) that divert collected fluids into the lined channels (photos #5 and 10) that then flow to the lined detention basin (photo #12). The drain tile piping outlets can be seen in photos #6 and 10. The "secondary" and "tertiary" emergency berms that were constructed following the release have been reworked (photo #8). The "tertiary" berm was determined to not have been impacted. The channel in the bottom of the "secondary" berm was excavated and impacted materials were removed.A water truck continues to collect fluids from the preexisting stormwater basin (photo #11) as necessary. Repsol plans to have a stationary pump brought in to pump fluids collected in the stormwater basin into the lined detention basin. A crew worked today to install a 4-inch line that will eventually pump fluids collected in the lined detention basin into a storage tank held on the pad surface. Fluids will only be held in the 4-inch line when pumping from the basin is ongoing. Three shallow, monitoring wells have been drilled downslope of the well pad to monitor the groundwater (see photo #14 for example). A fourth shallow, monitoring well is planned to be drilled in the adjacent field. Four deep, monitoring wells will also be drilled at the same locations as the shallow ones. Repsol reported that the first samples from the three monitoring wells already drilled may be collected today, 8/7.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301I departed the site at 1030 hours.

Comments: One November 13 2025, the Department conducted a complaint inspection in regards to a complaint submitted to the Department on 11/12/2025. Present during today's inspection was Matt Woods (DEP OGI).The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. There appeared to be an area along the access road with deep ruts beginning to form (photo 2). The Department recommends the operator ensure the access road is maintained. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.At the time of inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag and well posting was present at the time of thisinspection. There were no observed on going leaks or discharge of fluid on the ground or around the wellhead.Upon inspection of the production equipment, the Department observed severely corroded production lines running to/from the production tank. The corrosion has lead to large holes forming in the lines (photos 9-11). The Department did not observe any signs of a release from these corroded production lines. Soil conductivity readings were taken in the soil beneath the holes in the lines with readings of 0.27mS, and 0.17mS. These readings appeared comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.19mS.The production tank appeared to be sound with no visible leaks, however appeared to be empty. The Department recommends the operator remove the production tank if it is no longer necessary for production.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the corroded production lines.

Report Details
Inspection Client: BEECH RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/26/2024
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 8202741
Permit API: 081-21954
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/26/2024
Comments: On September 26, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the Beech Resources Delta Well Pad. No E and S issues were observed during the time of inspection. The site appeared to be stable and well vegetated meeting the 70% uniform perennial vegetative cover.Beech Resources contractors were in the process of setting up the well pad with production equipment and working on getting the AST ready for use. During the inspection, the east end of the well pad had some pools of water on it. The DEP screened the pool of water at the northeast corner with a conductivity meter. The conductivity meter measured the conductivity of the pool of water at 6,000 uS/cm. Near the pool of water in the northeast corner was a frack tank outside of containment. This frack tank contained water from the secondary containment of the drilling rig. Adjacent to the frack tank were multiple pallets of hoses used to manifold tanks together. The conductivity of the pool of water near and under the frack tank measured at 13,090 uS/cm. After observing the pools of water with elevated conductivity, the DEP went to the Company Man onsite and informed him of the findings. DEP showed the company where the pool of water was and the Company Man said that Beech Resources Don Stevenson was onsite. After finding Mr. Stevenson, DEP showed where the elevated conductivity pool was. Mr. Stevenson placed a call for a vac truck to mobilize to the well pad to removed the fluid. An excavator was used to dig a sump to collect the fluid so the vac truck could remove the fluid. Once the vac truck arrived onsite, Beech resources began removing the fluid from the sump and around the frack tank. The pallets of hoses were moved onto containment. During the removal of the fluid from the northeast corner conductivity was monitored in the fluid of the sump. Prior to DEP leaving the site, conductivity of the fluid in the sump measured at 3,900 uS/cm. Conductivity of the fluid was higher near the frack tank in the sump that was dug.At 1630 on September 26, 2024, Mr. Stevenson called DEP to inform them that all the fluid had been vacuumed and impacted soil had been removed. Mr. Stevenson said they were able to move the frack tank onto containment. After moving the frack tank, excavation of the impacted soil could begin. Mr. Stevenson said they removed approximately an excavator's bucket width for about 25 feet and removed about 6 inches of soil. Approximately 32 gallons of fluid was vacuumed and two roll off dumpsters were filled with impacted soil.Due to the amount of soil removed combined with the fluid vacuumed up Beech Resources has chosen to remediate to Act 2 standards. Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.66(b)1, Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted.

Comments: On 12/18/2025, Tim Sands reported a production fluid release from the Fabian Unit A3H well (063-37496). The spill was estimated to be greater than 5 gallons. Today (12/19/2025), I made a site visit. I met Rich Lightner onsite. The Fabian Well Pad had a rig onsite because XTO suspected that there was a hole in the tubing. As they pulled pipe, there was a production fluid release. The estimated release volume was 3.5 barrels (147 gallons). The incident happened at 11:00 am on 12/18/2025 and lasted approximately 9 minutes. XTO believes the release occurred due to a salt block. As the salt blocked dissolved, production fluid and gas was released from the piping. The spill area was isolated to the ground near the rig. No production fluid was discharged from the well pad.XTO marked the release area with flags and had a vacuum truck remove the production fluid from the ground on 12/18/2025. Overnight, it rained. There are now pools of water on the well pad.Due to the spill being greater than 42 gallons, the Department is requesting remediation and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Tipping receipts and waste manifests are requested by the Department associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from this spill.As I was leaving the well site, Melissa Breitenbach and Tim Sands called. XTO already contacted Moody and Associates about the cleanup. XTO plans on removing the rig from the site on Monday, 12/29/2025. Then, excavation and remediation will start the week of 1/5/2025. XTO will monitor the site and vacuum pooled water as needed. Violations are noted below.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8277572
Permit API: 123-47192
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2026
Comments: Evidence of stressed and dead vegetation in the vicinity of the Akins lease tank battery was visible from Rounds Hill Road. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection. This inspection was conducted to document findings of an apparent release of production fluids from the Akins tank battery, as well as a separate release from a brine tank previously removed from the nearby Loomis lease's tank battery. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners previously indicated that he had checked and found the integrity of the Loomis lease brine tank to be sufficient for future use. Kyle indicated that the tank was empty and would be unused until repurposed.The PVC drain line within the secondary containment area of the Akins tank battery was found to be improperly placed. The PVC line straddles the cutout hole in the surface of the brine tank in such a manner that fluids draining through the line would be able to flow over the surface of the brine tank and pool within the secondary containment area. Soil within secondary containment immediately below the PVC line was found to have specific conductance in excess of 17,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Evidence of pooling was visible in the containment area via crude oil staining and stressed vegetation. This indicates that fluid once filled the secondary containment, but apparently was able to migrate downward and/or outward through the secondary containment diking. Stressed and dead vegetation downslope and immediately outside the secondary containment dike further indicates the likelihood that the integrity of the secondary containment is inadequate. Understory vegetation was killed in an area approximately 30 feet wide by 200 feet long. Soils in the killzone were found to have elevated specific conductivity in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.The brine tank staged on location was found to have evidence of stressed and dead vegetation beginning from a point immediately beneath the drain valve and continuing downslope beyond the tank in an area approximately 10 feet wide by 200 feet in length. Specific conductivity in soils below the drain valve measured in excess of 8,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Soils in the killzone downslope of the brine tank were found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 micro Siemens per centimeter.Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Akins lease. The Akins Lease Akins 1 OG Well was found to have an illegible ID tag.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 6/06/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of the discovery of a release of an estimated 20 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and fresh water. According to the notification, fluid with electrical conductivity (EC) of 10-13 mS/cm was discovered on the pad surface in an area southeast of the well heads when secondary containment was removed from the pad surface. The notification also stated that a shallow trench has been dug along the southeast edge of the secondary containment to collect any additional fluid with elevated EC that may leach out from beneath the containment. The area impacted by the release was estimated to be 30 ft by 50 ft. I met with company man Steven Spitler upon arriving on location. It rained heavily during this inspection. The EC of the fluid present in the trench along the southeast edge of the well head secondary containment was between 4.03 mS/cm and 5.06 mS/cm. The 30 ft by 50 ft area of the pad surface reported to have been impacted by the release southeast of the well heads had puddles of fluid with EC readings between 2.48 mS/cm and 4.00 mS/cm. A vaccum truck was sucking up fluid from the impacted area of the pad surface during this inspection. Other areas of the pad surface had puddles of fluid with EC readings between 856 uS/cm to 1990 uS/cm. According to the company man, excavation of this area was going to be completed by Tobias Machining, present on site during this inspection, and characterization of the site would be conducted by Penn E and R who was en-route to the site during this inspection. The Department requests a justification for the estimated release volume. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up fluid with elevated EC from the pad surface. Violations noted against permit 081-21945 for the 6/6/24 reported release. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21946 for the 5/8/24 release discovered by the Department. These violations will be closed upon attainment of Act 2 remediation standards.

Comments: Site inspection conducted to review overall pad conditions following drilling at the Tract 726 Pad D. Meeting on site today with PGE Company Man David Waggoner. Weather conditions are sunny and 79 degrees following heavy precipitation in the previous 24 hours. According to Mr. Waggoner, PGE has completed drilling six new wells at This pad. Rigging down of the Precision 728 rig began on July 10th. Well stimulation activity is set to begin during the week of 7/22. There are no producing wells at this location. During this inspection a Costy's vacuum truck and crew are observed removing fluids from the remaining containment structure near the well cellars and from the remaining mud tanks at the west side of the pad (photos 2 and 6). STRAD tanks are being hauled off location. Rig mats are stacked along the north side of the pad and are being loaded onto amflatbed for removal (photo 5). Puddled fluid on site was screened using an Oakton PCTS 50 water conductivity meter and a Hanna Groline soil conductivity meter. While screening puddles around the north side of the containment structure, the Department observed fluid with elevated conductivity readings (2.5-3 mS/cm). Elevated conductivity readings indicate that a potential pollutional event may have occurred. Sample 4406-019 collected at 11:57 from fluid puddled on pad rock surface (photos 8 and 9). Sample will be analyzed using SAC 942. An unknown volume of fluid is observed in this area as it appears to extend under the containment structure (photos 3 and 8). Mr. Waggoner was informed of the sampling and the Department recommended vacuuming any free fluid from the pad surface as possible. Additional violations may be issued pending results of water sample analysis.

Report Details

Permit API: 083-52993
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-17
Comments: The operator contacted the Department on Monday, September 16 to report a spill that was found at the Warrant 5573 W87 well site. This site was previously impacted by a 10+ barrel spill that occurred 8/4/16 (ID #2509096). The operator at the time, SWEPI LP, has since sold the well to Pennhills Resources, who is currently operating the well. SWEPI LP is remediating the site under the Department's Oil and Gas Spill Policy. Present on site for this inspection were DEP ECB representative Barry Stanton, Pennhills Resources' Stuart and Tom Morris, and SWEPI LP's Pat Bernethy, and myself. An unknown, but likely small, volume of oil leaked from a line at the site and leached down through rock and into a seep on the hillside below. A small amount of oil was visible in two siphon dams constructed as containment just below the site, as well as in a channel leading to a previously constructed siphon dam. A small amount of this oil was found leaking into an UNT of a Chappel Fork that was previously impacted. The total length of impact from the spill site is approximately 400 horizontal feet. The operator has dug up the line to determine where the leak occurred, and is collecting oil on absorbent pads. Discussion was made regarding the responsibility of each party regarding remediation and reporting. Further inspection will be done on this site as necessary.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8249153
Permit API: 117-22252
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Richmond Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2025
Comments: On 9/19/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident/response to accident or event inspection at the Seneca Bechtel 674 well pad in Richmond TWP, Tioga County. This is in response to CTS 392369, describing the release of 10 gallons of diesel to the pad; the report received by the department on 9/18/2025. It was 63 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. The Site Act 9 sign, emergency response plan and PPC plan were located at the entrance to the access road. When I arrived on site, I met Seneca's HSE coordinator, Doug Tomlinson, who described the event as follows: Crews were on site installing production pipelines under the surface of the pad. Excavated material was being removed from trenches where the pipelines were being installed. The material was loaded onto a dump truck that was hauling the material to a stockpile on the northwest corner of the pad. While offloading the material onto the pile, workers believe that the front tire of the truck displaced a large rock that made contact with a pipe fitting on the side of the right diesel tank on the truck. This broke the fitting, the incident not noticed by the truck driver at that time. The driver drove approximately 300 feet from the pile of excavated material to the area where he was being loaded before somebody witnessed the diesel being released. The truck driver was stopped by a crew worker and the spill was contained. The release left a 300 foot path of spilled diesel that was approximately 8 inches wide with a larger pool where the truck stopped. The pipe fitting was on the fuel return line to the tank, The fitting has been repaired. The 300 feet of spilled material has been scraped up and loaded into a rolloff dumpster. The dumpster will be picked up by waste management and the material will be disposed when it has been properly characterized.The rock has been replaced along the 300 foot path but there was still a 10' x 10' area of the pad surface where the truck stopped that had not been filled in yet. While I was at the location, I did witness the dump truck offload excavated material onto the pile. Before the dump truck was allowed to drive on the pile to offload, a crew worker used an excavator to pack down the surface of the pile where the truck would drive. Pictures 10 through 14 were submitted by Seneca and show the impacted area, areas after being scraped, and the pad after clean stone was replaced.The pad is constructed to grade. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed around the site. Infiltration berms have been installed along the access road and the infiltration/MRC basin had been installed south of the pad. Most of the site is stabilized with at least 70% uniform perennial vegetation. Stabilization is becoming effective in recently disturbed areas. The temporary infiltration berm on the northwest corner of the pad has been removed. There are six wells permitted for the site at this time. The well cellars have been installed with the conductors scheduled to be installed on 9/22/2025. Current expectations for drilling is in 2026. The release of diesel fuel to the unprotected pad surface constitutes violations of these two regulations; SWMA 301 and CSL 402(b). The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends that Seneca personnel screen the area impacted by the release of diesel fuel for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Report Details
Inspection Client: APOLLO RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 1/12/2024
Violation Code: OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
Violation ID: 8171329
Permit API: 021-21026
Unconventional: No
County: Cambria
Municipality: Clearfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/12/2024
Comments: Follow up inspection of the County of Cambria Ivory 1 well conducted on 1/12/2024. Arrived on location at 10:03. Violations were issued on 3/23/2022, 9/22/2022, and 5/2/2023 site inspections for the following: OGA3220(A) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.91(a) - Failure to plug an abandoned well. 78.103 - Failure to monitor well granted Inactive Status on an annual basis and submit monitoring reports. 78.104 - Failure to meet the terms of Inactive Status. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect each well for compliance with requirements. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit Mechanical Integrity Report to the Department. OGA3211(G) - Failure to post the permit number and operators info at the well site. OGA3211(H) - Failure to install the permit number on the well upon completion in a permanent manner. This 1/12/2024 follow up inspection found that the well remains in a similar condition as the previous inspections. Violations were not addressed or responded to. Well is not equipped for production. Pumpjack, meter, and electric boxes remain on site. Much of the equipment has been dismantled. Wellhead is no longer tied inline. No permit number or operator ID found on the well. Wellhead and much of the equipment is overgrown with trees/brush. Well status was previously approved as Regulatory Inactive. Regulatory Inactive status expired on 04/20/2020. Operator failed to plug or return the well to active status. Review found no annual integrity monitoring reports submitted to the Department. Annual Production Reports have been submitted with 0 production shown for at least the last five years. All of the above violations remain outstanding.
